findings.reason: In the diff, `if (typeof iters[ii] === 'string') set.add(...)` is gone, and src/Set.js:107 now always calls SetCollection(iter). isArrayLike.js:2 returns true for strings, so `Set(['x']).union('abc')` now gives {'x','a','b','c'} where the baseline gave {'x','abc'}. Strings have no .size, so the filter at line 98 keeps them. List.js:145 still treats a string as one value, so List and Set now disagree. Kept high because the trigger is traced.
findings.claim: Removing the string special case in Set#union means a string argument on a non-empty Set is now split into its characters instead of being added as one value.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `if (typeof iters[ii] === 'string') { set.add(iters[ii]); } else {...}`. Line 107 now calls `SetCollection(iters[ii]).forEach(value => set.add(value))` for every argument. `isArrayLike` (src/utils/isArrayLike.js:2) returns true for `typeof value === 'string'`, so `maybeIndexedSeqFromValue` wraps a string in an ArraySeq of characters. Trigger: `Set(['x']).union('abc')` returned {'x','abc'} at baseline and now returns {'x','a','b','c'}. The sibling `List#concat` (src/List.js:145) still treats a string as a single value (`typeof argument !== 'string' && hasIterator(argument) ? argument : [argument]`), so the two collection APIs now disagree.
